head: d518ab6
target: Refuse a secret or model key shorter than 8 characters as a scenario problem before the first session opens, because a short value makes the scrub corrupt the run log.
incidental: the design-doc lines in docs/design/eval-scenarios.md that record the new rule and the exit-4 story

test fixtures: run.test.ts now sets a short secret and a short model key and expects their places in the refusal, and cli.test.ts's fake model key grew past 8 characters so the directory refusal stays the only problem
the MIN_SECRET_LENGTH constant and its comment in src/eval/run.ts

questions.prompt: A 1-character WEATHER_API_KEY broke a run after it had spent its model calls. What did that value do inside the run log?

options.label: The value stayed raw in the log, so the secret-free invariant found a leak in run.json
The provider refused the 1-character key at the first model call, so the run ended in error
The scrub replaced the value wherever it occurred, JSON keys included, so keys such as scenario became s[LEAKED:WEATHER_API_KEY]enario and the result directory no longer parsed
The runner treated the short value as unset, so the scenario lacked a secret it had named

key_points: the scrub replaces each raw value wherever it occurs in the log, JSON keys included
a 1-character value occurs inside ordinary words and key names, so it rewrote the log's structure, not just its text

questions.prompt: Before the fix, that same short key ended a run at exit 4. After it, the run exits 2 before any model call. Why did the failure surface so late before, and why so early now?

options.label: Exit 4 was the provider's own code for a rejected key; exit 2 is the runner's

The damage lands in the scrubbed log, and the run sees it only when it reads its result directory back to grade it; now the short value joins the other scenario problems, so the refusal comes before the first session opens
The model hid the short key in each reply, so only the grading at the end could see it
The fix moved the scrub before the first session, so an empty log is checked early

key_points: the CLI grades the files it just wrote, so the damage shows only when the run reads its result directory back
before the fix, nothing looked at the value's length: the run spent its model calls and failed at the read-back, an error no boundary named, which is exit 4
after the fix, the short value is a scenario problem reported with every other one, each at its place, and the refusal exits 2 before the first session opens

questions.prompt: The fix kept the scrub total: the raw value is still replaced wherever it occurs, JSON keys included. Which of these say why weakening the scrub, and keeping short secrets, would not have fixed the bug?

options.label: The scrub is content-blind: it marks every exact occurrence, leak or coincidence, so a short value still rewrites ordinary text in string values
The result-directory reader checks JSON keys for raw secrets, so a leak in a key is caught at grading
A raw value that lands in a JSON key would stay unmarked, so the log could hold a raw secret that the mark-based leak check never sees
Marks in ordinary text are harmless, because secret-free fails only on raw values

key_points: the scrub cannot tell an occurrence that is a real leak from one that is ordinary text, so a short value still rewrites whatever it lands in
the log must hold no raw value anywhere, keys included, and secret-free judges by marks, so an occurrence the scrub skips stays raw and invisible to the check
refusing the input keeps the scrub total and the invariant whole

questions.prompt: A teammate sets WEATHER_API_KEY to a 9-character word that also appears in the scenario's prompt text. What does the run do, and what does that say about what the 8-character rule guarantees?
key_points: the rule is a length threshold, not a judgment of content: a 9-character value passes, and the run opens sessions and spends its model calls
the scrub still replaces the value wherever it occurs, so the greeting in the log becomes a [LEAKED:WEATHER_API_KEY] mark
secret-free fails on any mark, so the run ends at a failed invariant, exit 1, not at an early refusal
the rule refuses the values most likely to collide with ordinary text; it lowers the odds of corruption, it does not promise that a value is safe
